messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 paging emily: production - runtime regression detected after recent release. High tail latency and increased 5xxs on inference pool A.

emily (oncall): on it — joining. can someone paste the deploy id?

deploy-bot: release_id=rel_2026_06_14_hotpatch_17, canary=10% -> full rollout at 03:12 UTC, config change: batch.max_window=200 -> 1000

raj (eng-runtime): that batch.max_window jump is suspicious. we pushed an optimization to increase batching window for throughput. canary metrics looked ok for small loads.

sofia (eng-sre): seeing a sharp drop in throughput on region-us-east-1, kernel fallback rate spiked to 42% on gpu-pool-03. 95th latency jumped from ~280ms to ~2.8s.

emily (oncall): customer-impact? are we seeing errors returned to callers?

sofia (eng-sre): yes — 502s/timeout errors increased ~1.7x in the last 8m for hostgroup inference-api-prod. A few customers opened support tickets complaining about timeouts.

michael (platform): logs show continuous prefetch eviction + KV cache churn. large batch windows are overflowing the runtime memory heuristic -> kernel fallback to CPU path on many instances.

raj (eng-runtime): that explains the latency. when fallback happens we lose optimized attention kernels and throughput collapses. need to kill the flag or revert fast.

emily (oncall): do we have a feature-flag for the new batching window?

raj (eng-runtime): yes, flag name: ff_runtime_batch_window_hotpatch. I can flip it immediately. flipping it to false will set batch.max_window back to 200.

emily (oncall): do it. also prepare rollback plan if flip doesn't improve within 3m. communicate to customers.

raj (eng-runtime): flipping flag now. 

raj (eng-runtime): ✅ flipped ff_runtime_batch_window_hotpatch -> false (propagated to 100% within ~20s).

sofia (eng-sre): monitoring... kernel fallback rate trending down to 6% on gpu-pool-03. 95th latency dropping toward 320ms. error rate normalizing.

emily (oncall): nice. start a canary re-check at 10% traffic for rel_2026_06_14_hotpatch_17 once we confirm stability.

michael (platform): can we add a temporary quota on batch.window via routing policy to prevent anyone overriding? I'll patch routing policy to enforce max 400 for 30m.

raj (eng-runtime): agreed. also rolling back the full rollout — set canary to stay at 10% and stop further progression.

deploy-bot: rollout-paused: rel_2026_06_14_hotpatch_17 canary preserved at 10%.

sofia (eng-sre): customer impact assessment: ~2.4k requests affected with >1s latency spikes, about 12 customers saw increased timeouts; no large-scale data loss. opened support ticket summary for outreach.

emily (oncall): great. assign followup: raj to prepare a patched hotfix with safer batching defaults + runtime guard, michael to enforce policy and add telemetry alert for kernel-fallback rate, sofia to coordinate customer comms and postmortem. I'll hand this to next on-call in 30m.

raj (eng-runtime): will draft fix and smoke test on staging. adding a canary automation check for kernel-fallback > 10% to block rollout.

michael (platform): patching routing policy now. applying temporary quota.

sofia (eng-sre): support notify sent. monitoring will validate for 45m before we consider full rollout.

emily (oncall): handing off to raj for the next 30m. raj, you'll be primary for the fix and canary gating. I’m offline for dinner at +30. if anything spikes above 10% kernel fallback or error rate > baseline*2, page SRE escalation channel.

raj (eng-runtime): acknowledged. will update channel with status and deployment plan.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated (primary mitigation applied: feature flag kill). severity: sev2 -> investigating followup.

emily (oncall): filing a brief incident note and start a postmortem template. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sofia (eng-sre): quick logs snippet from gpu-pool-03 during spike: ```
[2026-06-14T03:14:12Z] kernel_fallback=true reason=oom_heuristic batch_size=812 kv_cache_evictions=213
[2026-06-14T03:14:13Z] request_id=abc123 latency=2890ms status=502
```

raj (eng-runtime): useful. will add telemetry to capture batch_size distribution in next deploy.```
